Manufacturing Quality Performance & CAPA Status Summary
Ref: MQR-26-051 | Date: 04 May 2026 | From: Director, Manufacturing Excellence

Section 1. Defect Rate Overview by Product Line
During Q1 FY2026 (Jan–Mar), overall internal defect rate decreased to 2.1%, down from 3.4% in Q4 FY2025, representing a 38% reduction quarter-over-quarter. The Atlas Control Board line showed the most significant improvement, dropping from 4.8% to 2.6% following process stabilization in SMT Line 3. The Orion Sensor Module maintained steady performance at 1.3%, while the Vega Power Unit improved modestly from 2.9% to 2.2%. These results reflect targeted containment and sustained monitoring initiated in December.

Section 2. Root-Cause Analysis of Top Failure Modes
Pareto analysis identified three dominant failure modes accounting for 67% of total defects: solder bridging on QFN packages, torque nonconformance on enclosure fasteners, and intermittent PCB trace opens. The solder bridging issue was traced to stencil aperture wear and inconsistent paste deposition; corrective action included revised stencil inspection intervals and updated paste viscosity controls. Torque-related defects were linked to tool calibration drift on Station B-17, while PCB trace opens were primarily attributed to supplier laminate inconsistencies from Lot L-4582.

Section 3. Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Status
A total of nine CAPAs were opened in Q4 FY2025, of which seven are now verified and closed. CAPA-26-014 (Stencil Lifecycle Management) and CAPA-26-017 (Torque Tool Auto-Calibration Upgrade) demonstrated measurable impact, with defect recurrence reduced by over 60% in affected categories. Two preventive actions remain in progress, including implementation of automated optical inspection (AOI) parameter optimization and supplier process audits scheduled for May 2026. All actions are being tracked through the eQMS with weekly executive review.

Section 4. Customer Return and Field Performance Trends
Customer return rate (RMA per 1,000 units shipped) declined from 12.4 in Q4 FY2025 to 7.9 in Q1 FY2026. Notably, Atlas Control Board returns related to intermittent power loss dropped by 54% following rework containment and firmware validation updates. Warranty claim costs decreased by $184,000 compared to the previous quarter, reflecting improved outgoing quality and reduced field failures. No new systemic field issues were reported during the period.

Section 5. Sustained Control & Monitoring Plan
To maintain downward defect trends, Statistical Process Control (SPC) thresholds have been tightened for high-risk assembly stages, with automated alerts triggered at 1.5 sigma deviation. Monthly layered process audits will continue across SMT and final assembly operations. Additionally, supplier scorecards have been revised to incorporate first-pass yield metrics and corrective action responsiveness. Continued cross-functional review between Quality, Manufacturing, and Supply Chain is expected to further stabilize performance through FY2026.

text_content: **Defect Rate Performance by Product Line (Q1 2026 vs Q4 2025)**

The factory-wide defect rate improved from 2.8% in Q4 2025 to 2.1% in Q1 2026, representing a 0.7 percentage-point reduction and a 25% relative improvement in reported defects over the quarter. Stated differently, expected defects decreased from 28 per thousand units to 21 per thousand units on an aggregate basis. This quarter-over-quarter performance reflects consolidated data from all product lines and plant shifts for the January–March 2026 reporting period. The improvement materially reduces downstream rework and inspection load and establishes a new baseline for Manufacturing Operations as of 31 March 2026. These metrics will be included in the April 2026 executive performance review and prioritization immediately.

Line-level analysis for Q1 2026 shows divergent performance across product families. Product Line A recorded a defect rate of 1.6% in Q1 2026, placing it well below the factory average and demonstrating consistent quality control at the line level. By contrast, Product Line C recorded a defect rate of 2.9% in Q1 2026, above the facility aggregate and warranting targeted monitoring given its relative position. These two lines account for distinct manufacturing processes and product specifications; their performance variance materially affects aggregate results and will be highlighted in product-line scorecards circulated to Supply Chain and Sales teams in April 2026 for executive review and prioritization immediately.

From an operational perspective, the shift to a 2.1% factory defect rate as of 31 March 2026 reduces forecasted warranty exposure and improves first-pass yield projections for Q2 2026. The 0.7 percentage-point decrease versus Q4 2025 is sufficiently large to be considered operationally significant and will inform monthly KPI thresholds maintained on the Manufacturing Dashboard beginning April 2026. Control-chart monitoring will continue with weekly sampling at each production line; lines exceeding 2.5% will trigger enhanced supervision and capacity reallocation. Planned next steps include updated line-level targets for Q2 2026, a refined sampling plan, and monthly reporting to Executive Operations on the 15th of each month for review.

sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.body: During the January–April 2026 reporting period, overall internal defect rates across all product lines declined to 2.1%, down from 3.4% in Q4 2025. This 38% reduction correlates directly with targeted root-cause corrective actions implemented in late 2025 and reinforced through structured CAPA reviews. The most significant improvements were observed in the Atlas Control Module and NovaDrive Assembly lines. Customer return volumes have also trended downward for three consecutive months, indicating improved field reliability.

sections.heading: Defect Rates by Product Line
sections.body: The Atlas Control Module line recorded a defect rate of 1.6%, reduced from 3.1% in the prior quarter, primarily due to stabilization of the automated solder reflow process. The NovaDrive Assembly line improved from 4.2% to 2.5% after torque calibration protocols were standardized across all shifts. In contrast, the Helix Sensor Unit line showed a modest reduction from 2.8% to 2.4%, with intermittent failures still linked to supplier component variability. Scrap costs decreased by approximately $184,000 quarter-over-quarter as a result of these improvements.

sections.heading: Root-Cause Analysis of Top Failure Modes
sections.body: The leading failure mode in Q4 2025—cold solder joints in Atlas boards—was traced to inconsistent thermal profiles caused by uneven oven zone calibration. Corrective action included recalibration of all eight reflow ovens and installation of inline thermal monitoring sensors. For NovaDrive units, stripped fasteners were attributed to manual torque variation, which has since been mitigated through deployment of digital torque drivers with lockout thresholds. On the Helix line, micro-cracks in housing assemblies were linked to over-clamping during ultrasonic welding; process parameters have been revised and operator retraining completed.

sections.heading: CAPA Implementation and Status
sections.body: A total of 17 CAPAs were opened between November 2025 and February 2026, of which 14 have been fully verified and closed. The remaining three CAPAs relate to supplier corrective actions for the Helix Sensor Unit and are pending final validation audits scheduled for mid-May. All closed CAPAs underwent effectiveness verification through a minimum 30-day defect monitoring window. Compliance with CAPA documentation timelines improved from 72% to 96%, reflecting stricter review cadence and accountability measures.

sections.heading: Customer Return Trends and Field Performance
sections.body: Customer return rates decreased from 1.9% in December 2025 to 1.1% in April 2026 across all shipped units. Warranty claims related to electrical intermittency dropped by 41%, particularly for Atlas modules shipped after process stabilization in January. Average turnaround time for returned material authorization (RMA) processing improved from 12 days to 8 days due to revised triage workflows. The positive field data supports the conclusion that corrective actions have effectively reduced systemic manufacturing defects.

Ref: MQ-26-041 | Date: 22 April 2026 | From: Director of Quality Assurance

Section Executive Summary
During Q1 2026, overall plant defect rate decreased to 1.82%, down from 2.47% in Q4 2025, representing a 26% quarter-over-quarter improvement. The most significant reductions were observed in the ApexDrive motor assembly line and the Orion control module line following targeted corrective actions. This report outlines the primary root causes identified, the status of CAPA initiatives, and correlated trends in customer returns. Performance improvements are directly linked to disciplined containment and process control enhancements implemented since January.

Section Defect Rates by Product Line
ApexDrive motor assemblies recorded a defect rate of 1.35%, reduced from 2.10% in the prior quarter, largely due to improvements in coil winding calibration. Orion control modules showed a decline from 3.02% to 2.11%, primarily driven by solder joint process stabilization. The NovaFlex harness line remained stable at 0.98%, maintaining the lowest defect incidence across all product families. Remaining elevated scrap in Orion units is concentrated in surface-mount misalignment, currently under active mitigation.

Section Root-Cause Analysis of Top Failure Modes
The top failure mode in Q4 2025 was intermittent motor torque loss, traced to inconsistent varnish curing temperatures in Oven 3 at the Dayton facility. Installation of calibrated thermal sensors and revised preventive maintenance intervals reduced related defects by 63% in Q1. For the Orion line, cold solder joints were linked to fluctuating reflow oven conveyor speeds; updated PLC controls and operator retraining have stabilized the process. No systemic material supplier defects were identified during this review period.

Section Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Status
Of the 18 CAPAs opened between November 2025 and February 2026, 14 have been fully implemented and verified for effectiveness. The remaining four actions, focused on automated optical inspection (AOI) false-negative rates, are scheduled for completion by 30 May 2026. Weekly cross-functional audits have improved closure cycle time from an average of 46 days to 28 days. Evidence of sustained compliance is being tracked through layered process audits and monthly KPI dashboards.

Section Customer Return Trends
Customer return rate decreased to 0.74% of shipped units in Q1, compared with 1.12% in Q4 2025. Warranty claims related to torque irregularities dropped by 41%, aligning with internal defect reductions. Two major OEM clients reported measurable improvement in first-pass yield at their assembly sites using ApexDrive components. Continued monitoring of field performance data will determine whether current improvements are sustained through the next production cycle.

text_content: **Top Failure Modes, CAPA Execution Status, and Customer Return Trend Impact**

Failure Mode FM-01 (Solder voids) accounted for 34% of Q1 2026 defects. Root-cause analysis conducted by the NPI and Quality Engineering teams identified three contributing factors: 1. inconsistent solder paste volume at stencil-to-board interface, 2. suboptimal reflow profile during hot zone ramp, and 3. entrapped flux volatiles. Field and process audits validated the solder void correlation with a single-wave supplier lot and with PCB design pad geometry on two product families.

Corrective and preventive actions were prioritized to address FM-01 and associated modes. CAPA-2026-014 was opened on 2026-02-12 and is currently In Verification. Actions under this CAPA include stencil design revision, supplier qualification for solder paste lot traceability, and updated reflow profile verification. Additional CAPAs addressing solder cleaning and design changes are in Implementation or Completed states. Verification metrics include x-ray void rate reduction targets and process capability improvement thresholds.

The customer return trend reflects early impact of corrective measures: customer return rate decreased from 1.2% in January 2026 to 0.9% in March 2026. Supply chain and customer service teams report reduced field complaints for the affected product families, correlating with pilot process changes implemented in February. Ongoing monitoring will use monthly return rate, field failure detail, and warranty cost metrics to assess CAPA effectiveness, with escalation criteria defined for any reversal of the downward trend and executive oversight.
